newsitem.title: UK: BA cancels day's Gatwick short-haul flights.
newsitem.headline: BA cancels day's Gatwick short-haul flights.

text.p: British Airways Plc has abandoned plans to operate any short-haul flights out of London Gatwick on Monday but said it still hoped to get four inter-continental services away, now the airport has been re-opened following a bomb alert.
London's second biggest airport was closed early on Monday along with several major rail stations and roads around London by a fresh round of suspected Irish Republican Army (IRA) bomb threats.
BA said it has cancelled a total of 108 flights out of Gatwick today, including 72 European and domestic and 13 long-haul flights, as well as a further 23 shorthaul services operated by franchisees.
It still hoped to operate the day's four remaining longhaul services, to Buenos Aires, Sao Paulo/Santiago, to Harare/Lusaka and Nairobi/Entebbe.
But the airline said it now needed to concentrate on getting its shorthaul fleet in position for operating a normal service on Tuesday.
BA normally flies around 22,000 passengers a day in and out of Gatwick on a typical weekday, the airline said.

"The decision to cancel the airline's shorthaul mainline programme was taken because of shortages of ground staff and air crew caused by the continuing congestion on the roads to the airport, coupled with the dispersion of aircraft that would normally operate these services around airfields across southern England," BA said in a statement.

It said many of today's inbound flights to Gatwick had also been cancelled or diverted to other airports around the country, including London Heathrow, Birmingham, Bournemouth, Southampton, Cardiff, London Stansted and Manston in Kent.
